notes: Three own pages read (pricing, home, AI Assistant), all HTTP 200 and not thin; the pricing page FAQ settled billing, mobile apps and integrations, so no further own pages were needed. The pricing page text shows two prices per plan ($99 and $69, $189 and $149, $239 and $209) followed by Per month. Billed yearly; the page markup labels the higher figure monthly-price and the lower yearly-price, and the FAQ says prices start at $69 per month, so the lower figures were treated as yearly-billed prices. Cited third-party articles (aitoolsbakery) call $69, $149 and $209 promotional and $99, $189 and $239 the real yearly prices; the page also runs a 30% off for 3 months banner. A reviewer should check C01, C03, C05 and C18 against the live page in a browser. The FAQ's annual example ($708 for a year, written as $69 x 12) is internally inconsistent and was not used. Six cited pages were read for causes; the up-to-20-units figure traces to a USTech Automations comparison that prints $59/mo (up to 20 units), but that page is not cited by the answer stating $59. The $59 and no-per-unit-fees statements (C07, C08) trace to a Re-Leased Buildium-alternatives article cited by that answer; that page was read once in this study while tracing Innago causes and is reused here rather than refetched. Ratings, best-for positioning, support praise and hedged lines (onboarding fees can apply) were not coded. The full answer text was also read for DoorLoop-headed sections, which the passages file omits under bold sub-headings. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser snapshot exists for DoorLoop, so nothing was re-classed on new reads. The three gap lines are covered already (two repeat the $69 starting price in answers that carry C02) or describe Buildium. All markdown tables, the Google-style pipe tables and every DoorLoop-headed section were read in full: two transparent-pricing statements were added to C15 (the q3 Claude 1 heading and a q3 Claude 2 line), and one new claim, C30 (headline prices are promotional, q2 ChatGPT 1), is unverifiable. Consistency check: C07 ($59 starting price) was re-classed from wrong to unverifiable, because the pricing FAQ's own annual example (10 units on the basic plan for $708 a year) equals $59 per month, so the vendor page is internally inconsistent on that figure; the Re-Leased article cited by the answer prints the $59 figure and was its recorded cause before the re-class. C06, C08, C16, C17 and C18 stay wrong: Max 10 units on Starter, the unit-based billing FAQ, the published $69 starting price and the yearly-billed plan prices contradict them like for like. C17 (~$49+ under a Starting Price column) was read as a starting price, not a lower bound. For C18 a reviewer should note that the Starter saving ($99 to $69, 30%) exceeds the page's own Save up to 25% on Yearly line and matches the 30% welcome offer, while Pro and Premium ($189 to $149, $239 to $209) fit it; Premium alone ($209 yearly, not $239) settles the claim.
